dependencies.reason: On Bevy, core.scene loads the native part of the scenes, as a plugin. Godot, Unity and Unreal have their own scenes, driven by their gateway.

provides.description: The engine contract kits require (game.engine@^1): version, active(), content, scenes, scripts, flow.
Rust KitHost only: bounded decisions, resolution playback, replay libraries, diagnostics and absolute presentation. Legacy engine scripts do not provide this capability.

Game life cycle: phase(), start(scene?, entry?), end(result), restart(), result(). 1.1 (game.engine 1.9): with a title that shows the game (ui.menu titleMode scene), phase() is title until Play while the start scene is staged behind it, held.

Content registry; placeGround(entity) queues a spawn query, with engine.placement.completed and engine.placement status/warnings. registerComponent(name, handler, kit), instances(scene?), instance(id) (with its talk topic), reflection(id), reflections(), entityOf(id), instanceOf(entity), archetype(id), state(id), setState(id, patch), report(), compiled(), active().

Scenes: current(), pending() (the scene the start will open, from setup), list(), enter(scene, entry?), visited(). sceneExit views carry next. 1.2 (game.engine 1.7): info(scene?) → { id, kind, role, next, title, loading, background, implicit, world, native, transition, below }, enter(scene, entry?, { unload, previous: { visible, paused } }) keeps the scene left loaded, push(scene, { entry, below, active }), pop(scene?), unload(scene), set(scene, { visible, paused }), stack(), active(), activate(scene), worldShown(), levels(), menu(), next(scene?), advance(entry?), loading() → { from, to, entry, ratio, since } | null, assets(scene?) (its scene_assets list, else computed). 1.3 (game.engine 1.11): native scenes, both ways — nativeEntered(path, { mode: replace | additive, kind, entry, assets }) → { scene, adopted, entered, known } (an engine adapter tells a native scene the game put in by itself; a path no document names is adopted as a scene of the game), nativeLeft(path), nativeAssets(scene, deps) (its files from the engine's dependency list), nativeScene(path) → scene id; info(scene).adopted. 1.4 (game.engine 1.19): the loading steps of the game — holdStep(id, { label?, scene?, timeout? }) (work of the game the kits cannot see, its terrain, its generation: without scene it holds the whole game, Play waits and a scene being entered waits behind its screen; with scene, or scene: "current", it holds that scene: its loading waits, and once entered its screen stays and entering() is true), stepProgress(id, ratio), releaseStep(id) → boolean, steps(scene?) → [{ id, label, scene, ratio }]; variable engine.steps { pending, game, ratio, label }; a step drops after its timeout (120 s by default).
Script verbs: registerAction(name, decl, fn, kit), registerCondition(…), verbs(), rules(), enable(script), disable(script), played().

Interceptable decisions: decide(hook, payload) → { ok, payload, cancelled, reason, by, notes } (run is the same method), hold(hook, key, payload) / release(hook, key?) / held() for a continuous decision, tap(hook, fn, { priority, owner, id }) → id (an undeclared hook or a taken id is an error), untap(id) → bool, declare(hook, { mutable, cancellable, fields }, owner) (one owner per hook), declared(), taps(hook?), orphans(), problems(). Taps run by priority (higher first, 0 by default), then registration: the last has the final word, whoever registered it. Each tap sees the payload the previous ones left and the decision so far ({ cancelled, reason, by }, third argument); it answers { set, cancel: true|false, reason, stopImmediate }. Asked only when a tap listens.

The mods the game was mounted with: list(), applied(), has(id), originOf(collection, id), fingerprint() (1.3: a stable string for the mods applied and their content, '' without a mod; network kits compare it in their handshake).

1.3: what can be plugged into a kit, names only (hooks, events emitted and listened, registries, collections, config, moddable and live, settings, verbs, components, services, completeness counts): list() for the installed kits, of(kit) for any kit of the catalogue. The full view with schemas is extensionPointsOf(manifest).

Named zones exist without a world kit: the scene zones and the project zones collection, in the host zones (ctx.zones). No service of its own: a world kit that also provides world.zones (city block, district, rooms) serves its view.

What game.engine shows the debugger (debug.expose@1): epoch(), scenes(), instances(), vars(), hooks(), mods(), archetypes(). Called by debug.inspector only, while its panel is open or a snapshot is asked.

startScene.description: Scene to start in (default: the first scene, or the implicit scene of a project without scenes).

startEntry.description: Entry of the start scene (default: its first entry).

title.description: on: wait on the ui.menu title screen (Play) before entering the start scene.

shapes.description: The values a simple shape (model.shape) takes for a size it leaves out; a scene or a mod changes them like any config.

material.description: The material of a simple shape for a field it leaves out (over a model file, a material only replaces what it gives).

texture.description: Texture keys of the game (a path of its assets, or a slot it binds): color, normal, metallicRoughness (glTF: metal blue, roughness green).

materials.description: Named materials, reused by name (asset.material, model.material, set_material).

texture.description: Texture keys of the game (a path of its assets, or a slot it binds): color, normal, metallicRoughness (glTF: metal blue, roughness green).

placement.description: Spawn placement queries active engine collisions. The legacy baked setting is accepted but no longer samples terrain or uses cached coordinates.

enabled.description: false: no mod is applied to this game.

order.description: Application order (the others follow in document order); a mod always comes after the mods it depends on.

deny.description: What the mods of this game may not touch, among what the kits declare moddable.

story.description: Story flags: { "lantern_found": false } → story.lantern_found variables, saved with the game.

menu.description: scene: the title screen of ui.menu is a scene of its own, entered first with no world behind it (the project's role: menu scene, else one synthesised: menu); Play leads to the start scene. overlay: the title is drawn over the start scene (before 1.7). Every project gets scene once it is opened (autoUpdateProject) and every new game is made with it.

menuScene.description: The menu scene, when several interface scenes exist.

loading.description: How a scene whose files are not in yet waits: ui.menu's loading screen, the loading scene, nothing, or background (the scene left stays until the next one is ready).

loadingScene.description: Id of the scene of kind loading shown between two scenes when loading is scene (default: the first such scene, else one synthesised).

loadTimeout.description: Seconds a scene waits for its files before it is entered anyway.

minLoadingMs.description: Shortest time a loading screen stays, in milliseconds (0: only while files load).

unload.description: release: leaving a scene frees its instances and the memory of the files only it used (never the disk cache, never a preload asked elsewhere).

transition.description: How a scene comes in when neither it nor the call says: replace (the scene left is unloaded) or add (it stays loaded under the new one).

showAfterMs.description: A loading screen comes up only when the files of the next scene are still not in after this many milliseconds (preloaded or cached files: no screen at all, no flash).

onFail.description: A file of the next scene failed: retry (up to retries, then enter), enter (go on without it) or wait (until engine.scenes.retry() or cancelLoading()).

retries.description: How many times onFail retry asks the files that failed again.

image.description: An illustration shown while the scene loads.

tips.description: Tips shown one at a time (i18n.text keys preferably).

image.description: An image filling the loading screen.

video.description: A muted video looping behind the loading screen.

color.description: The colour behind the loading screen (#rrggbb).

background.description: The backdrop of the loading screen.

title.description: The title shown (default: the title of the scene loading).

loadingScreen.description: 1.7: the dressing of a loading screen (overlay or loading scene).

hz.description: The logic tick in Hz, the game maker's choice (strategy 10-20, action 30, twitch shooter 60): kit logic, actions and timers run at this fixed rate, decoupled from the frame rate (the render loop interpolates between the last two ticks) and from the physics step (its own 1/60 s). Live: a change (config, runtime.core.tickAdjust({ hz }), the F9 panel) takes effect at the next tick boundary, nothing reset. Not moddable: every peer of a match plays the same tick; in a match only the authority changes it.

maxCatchUp.description: Optional cap on the ticks one frame may catch up. 0 (default): no cap, every due tick is played (one frame hands the clock 0.25 s at most, so a stall never spirals). A number: past it the rest of the time is dropped. Only the tick fed from the frame (source "frame") accumulates ticks; on the physics step of an engine the engine's own catch-up applies (Godot max_physics_steps_per_frame).

source.description: Who counts the action tick. "independent" (default, every engine and network included): the TickClock runs on real time, so the actions keep their pace if the physics slows down; the ticks due are played at the first callback the engine offers (Godot _process), with no cap unless maxCatchUp is set. "engine-physics": the action tick is counted from the physics loop of the engine (Godot _physics_process, Unity FixedUpdate), with its fixed step, never the frame time; it slows down with the physics. Characters move correctly in both (they use the step of the loop they run in).

physicsHz.description: The physics step of the engine in Hz. 0 (default): when the game sets tick.hz and syncPhysics is on, the physics follows tick.hz; otherwise the engine setting is left alone. A number: the host sets it (Godot physics_ticks_per_second, Unity fixedDeltaTime). The characters move with the physics step, never with the frame time.

syncPhysics.description: Align the engine physics step with tick.hz when the game sets tick.hz and physicsHz is 0. Off: the physics keeps the engine setting.

interpolate.description: Render interpolation between two ticks (alpha, tick_alpha()). Off: the latest tick is shown as is.

systems.description: Every-N periods of the kit systems, by "<kit>.<system>": a number of ticks, or { every, offset, hz } (offset: the phase, spread by name by default). Example { "npc.core.decide": 3, "stealth.detection.perceive": 2 }. Combat hit resolution stays every tick.

tick.description: The logic tick (docs/game-engine-contract.md « Boucle de tick et boucle de rendu »).

thread.description: Where the action loop (the TickClock and the ticks of the kits) runs. "main" (default): on the main thread of the engine, in its callbacks (Godot _process). "own": on a thread of its own on a computer (a Web Worker with shared memory on the web): the main thread reads the presented state in place and never waits for a tick; the physics stays the engine's, on its own thread when it can, and is asked through the ordered queue and the tickets of the physics (ask_move_character / poll_moved); what must run on the main thread (scene, nodes, _action_process, signals) is played at the next callback of the engine with its tick number, at most one frame later. When the host cannot (no threads, a page that is not cross-origin isolated, a GDScript service or tap the kits call during the tick, tick.source engine-physics) it stays on "main" and says why (F9 TICK, tick_info().threadWhy). Godot today; Unity, Unreal and Bevy keep "main".

action.description: The action loop (docs/game-engine-contract.md « Boucle de tick et boucle de rendu », action.thread).

emits.description: The description of the reflection of an instance (docs/entites-et-rendu.md): told at its spawn and when a display verb changes its render (play_clip, set_morph, set_material, setFade). The presentation module resolves it against the states of the entity; never written in the entity, never saved.
The derived states the table state → reflection of an instance reads, when they change (checked each tick, only for the instances whose rules or bound values read one).

The fade of an instance by its distance to the camera changed (setFade): { start, end, mode? } it shows now (null: none). Once per change; an engine applies it natively (by alpha by default: Bevy the alpha of a copy of its material, Godot the material's distance fade; mode dither: Bevy VisibilityRange, Godot visibility range).
1.23: the material of an instance changed (set_material): the whole material it shows now (null: the file's own). Once per change; an engine changes the drawn object's material in place.
The morph weights of an instance changed (set_morph): the whole set, 0..1 per shape. Once per change, never per frame; the gateways apply it to blend shapes / morph targets.
One spawn ground query completed: applied or skipped with structured warnings. Authored storey is preserved; no available floor leaves the pose unchanged.
1.3: a tap of mission.complete refused the end of a mission (reason and tap id; both may be null). The mission stays active.

A scene was entered (instances spawned, kits ran sceneEnter). Only with engine content, or a title that is a scene of its own. 1.7: kind (and implicit) in a game with a scene flow; resumed when a scene kept loaded comes back, stacked when it was added on others. 1.9: staged when the scene is entered behind a title that shows the game (built and drawn, the game time held, its rules not armed), then entered again without staged when Play hands it over (no rebuild, no respawn): a listener that starts gameplay skips staged.
The current scene is about to be left. 1.7: kind of the scene left; kept when it stays loaded (hidden, paused or both).
1.7: emitted when the loading screen of a scene comes up (its files were not ready after showAfterMs): the mode (overlay, a scene id) and its dressing (image, tips, background).
1.7: emitted when the loading of a scene moves (a file in, or 10 % more): the progress asset.preload gives for it, never a simulated bar.
1.7: emitted when files of the scene being loaded failed, with what follows (retry, enter, wait).

1.7: emitted when the change to a scene does not happen and is not an error. Given up: reason cancel (cancelLoading) or replaced (another change), no by. Cancelled on purpose (by, never empty, says who; reason says why): a tap of engine.scene.change or a hook of asset.preload (wantScene / retryScene answer { refused: { by, reason } }); the current scene stays, no failure screen, no new try. An error (a file missing, a preload that fails) is engine.scene.failed.
1.7: emitted when a scene is added on the scenes loaded (push_scene, engine.scenes.push): what those under it do (run, pause, hide).
1.7: emitted when a loaded scene is taken off (pop_scene, engine.scenes.pop): it is unloaded; the scene under it comes back if it was the active one.
1.7: emitted when another loaded scene becomes the active one (inputs, new instances, current()).

1.7: emitted when the states of a loaded scene change: hidden or shown, paused (frozen: instances tagged paused, no collider, no zone, its sounds stopped; the game time stops when every loaded world is paused) or running.
1.7: a scene change was accepted and the next scene loads: loading says how it shows (a loading scene id, overlay, none — none when its files are already in).
1.19: emitted when the game holds a loading step of its own (engine.scenes.holdStep, GfGameHost.hold): without scene the whole game waits for it (Play, a scene being entered), else that scene.
1.19: emitted when the game moves the progress of a step (engine.scenes.stepProgress).
1.19: emitted when the work of a step is done (engine.scenes.releaseStep): what it held goes on.
1.19: emitted when a step was held longer than its timeout (120 s by default) and dropped: what it held goes on.
1.7: emitted when the files of the next scene are in (or loadTimeout passed), right before it is entered.
1.7: a scene left was freed: its instances destroyed, the memory of the files only it used released (the disk cache stays).
The title screen is shown (flow.title on, a menu scene, or 1.9 a title that shows the game: scene is the scene staged behind it).
The game ended (won, lost or a custom result).
The game restarted from its start scene.
The player used an instance (scripts: { "interact": "self" }).
set_state changed an instance state.
play_clip.
set_solid.
show / hide.
An instance spawned.
The game was mounted with mods (only when the project has mods documents).
A save made with other mods was loaded.

1.3: a reaction (an action of a rule) was refused: its target is not open or not live, the value does not fit the schema, or the rule is caught in a loop (beyond 8 generations of events in a row). Nothing else stops.
1.3: a reaction changed a document of a live collection (the kit that owns it reads it again).
1.3: a reaction changed a live config path of a kit.
A tap wrote what the hook does not allow (not_mutable, invalid, not_cancellable): that write was left out.
end_game with the result won (the flow then ends: engine.flow.ended).
end_game with the result lost.
A call verb found no such service method.

listens.description: 1.9: the host enters playing (end of the mount, a countdown over) while a scene is staged behind the title: the time is held again.

kind.description: Spawn factory: prop (game.engine), npc (npc.core), player, vehicle, or a kind a kit or game code registers. Default prop.

slot.description: An existing slot, or content:<archetype id>.

item.description: Library item (lib_…): bound to the slot content:<archetype id>.

shape.description: A simple shape drawn instead of a file, built by each engine with its own primitive meshes (docs/game-engine.md « Formes simples »).

size.description: box [x, y, z], plane [x, z]; one number: a cube or a square.

radius.description: sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone (base), torus (centre to the middle of the tube).

tube.description: torus: the radius of the tube.

color.description: Base colour: #rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa (sRGB) or [r, g, b(, a)] in 0..1; an alpha below 1 blends.

doubleSided.description: Drawn on both sides (default: a plane only).

material.description: The material: the name of one of the config's materials, or a material (colour, textures, metal, roughness, emission, alpha, unlit, double sided, UV repeat). On a file, it replaces only what it gives.

texture.description: Texture keys of the game (a path of its assets, or a slot it binds): color, normal, metallicRoughness (glTF: metal blue, roughness green).

components.description: Component name → value. Each name is claimed by a kit (engine.components of its manifest) or owned by game.engine (state, solid, model, size, model.placement, entry).

offer.description: Dialogue id offered before the quest starts (one of its choices runs start_mission).

thanks.description: Dialogue when the quest comes back to this NPC (its talk_to step) and after it.

gives.description: This NPC gives this quest: compiled to rules over the dialogue topics.

clips.description: Logical clip name → animation clip of the model (play_clip: "open").

extends.description: 1.3: inherit every key of this archetype that this one does not write (resolved before the kits mount).

native.description: A native engine scene (res://….tscn, Assets/….unity, /Game/…): its nodes are the instances.

config.description: The world kit config for this scene.

doc.description: A document of the world kit collection (runs, race_tracks, terrain_maps…).

set.description: Component overrides, merged over the archetype component by component.

offer.description: Dialogue id offered before the quest starts (one of its choices runs start_mission).

thanks.description: Dialogue when the quest comes back to this NPC (its talk_to step) and after it.

gives.description: This NPC gives this quest: compiled to rules over the dialogue topics.

resolved.description: Deprecated legacy placement; runtime ignores these cached coordinates.

data.description: Per-scene sections of the collections kits declare in engine.sceneCollections.

items.description: A panel served by core.webui: { id, page, bind, open }.

scripts.description: Scripts that belong to this scene (catalogue; every script compiles).

kind.description: 1.7: what the scene is — 3d (default), 2d, interface (no world: title, main menu, credits; kits build nothing, the renderers draw no world), loading (shown while the next scene loads), cinematic.

role.description: 1.7: its part in the game — menu (entered first, Play leads on), level (levels follow the document order), credits, other.

next.description: 1.7: the scene that follows (Play from a menu, the end of a level, the verb next_scene). Default: the next level.

loading.description: 1.7: how the loading of this scene shows when its files are not ready: overlay (ui.menu's loading screen), none, background (the scene left stays until this one is ready), or a scene id (a loading scene, or an interface scene of the game: its own screen).

scene.description: A light 3D scene drawn behind the interface.

background.description: 1.7: the backdrop of an interface scene.

unload.description: 1.7: what leaving the scene frees: release (default) or keep.

transition.description: 1.7: how load_scene / next_scene bring it in: replace (the scene left is unloaded) or add (stacked: the scene left stays loaded). Default: sceneFlow.transition.

below.description: 1.7: added on others, what the scenes under it do: run (go on, drawn), pause (drawn, frozen), hide (not drawn, still running).

image.description: An illustration shown while the scene loads.

tips.description: Tips shown one at a time (i18n.text keys preferably).

image.description: An image filling the loading screen.

video.description: A muted video looping behind the loading screen.

color.description: The colour behind the loading screen (#rrggbb).

background.description: The backdrop of the loading screen.

title.description: The title shown (default: the title of the scene loading).

loadingScreen.description: 1.7: the dressing of a loading screen (overlay or loading scene).

on.description: Scope: an instance id, archetype:<id>, scene:<id>, or absent (global).

enabled.description: false: compiled but off until enable_script.

when.description: A DSL condition or a sugar: interact, enter, leave, scene, talked, quest, state.

items.description: Actions: DSL, engine verbs (set_state, play_clip, set_solid, show, hide, enable_script, disable_script, load_scene, end_game, call, set_talk, set_morph), kit verbs, shorthands { verb: arg }.
Actions when `when` holds and `if` does not.

once.description: Play the rule once per game (saved).

hook.description: The hook tapped (engine.hooks of a kit manifest): trade.shop.buy.

priority.description: Higher runs first; the lowest has the last word. Default 0.

match.description: Payload fields that must equal these values.

items.description: Conditions of the trigger DSL that must all hold (the payload is the event payload).

set.description: Mutable field → value (1.3: a computed value { "$field" | "$var" | "$add" | "$mul" … }).

add.description: Mutable numeric field → number added (1.3: or a computed value).

mul.description: Mutable numeric field → factor (1.3: or a computed value, { "$var": "difficulty" }).

min.description: Mutable numeric field → lower bound (1.3: or a computed value).

max.description: Mutable numeric field → upper bound (1.3: or a computed value).

patch.description: 1.3, a mutable list or object field → { set?, append?, remove?, update? }: the operations of a mod patch, on the field: append / remove / update take a list (the field itself) or { "<path inside the field>": … }, set merges keys into an object field.

reason.description: Why it was cancelled: handed back to the kit.

stopImmediate.description: The taps after this one are not asked.

id.description: Mod id, unique in the project.

requires.description: Kit id → version range the mod was made for ({ "game.engine": "^1.2", "trade.shop": "^1" }).

optional.description: true: applied after that mod when it is there, applied anyway when it is not.

config.description: Kit id → { key: value }: config keys the kit declares moddable.

configPatch.description: 1.3, kit id → { set, append, update, remove } by dotted path, under keys or paths the kit declares moddable.

data.description: Collection → { add, patch, remove }: documents of collections their kit declares moddable.

center.description: World position of the zone center

watch.description: Entity tags the zone watches (default player)

generated.description: ISO date of the last generation.

id.description: A slot of the game, a path, or a logical id (world:<kit>, kit:<hud>, audio:<name>).

shared.description: Used by other scenes too: leaving this one does not free it.

source.description: generated: rewritten by the next refresh; manual: kept.

loading.description: overlay, none, background (loaded behind, shown once ready) or a scene id.

push_scene.description: 1.7: add a scene on the scenes loaded (they stay: run, pause or hide); it becomes the active one unless active is false.

pop_scene.description: 1.7: take a loaded scene off and unload it (default: the active one; the scene under it comes back).

set_scene.description: 1.7: the states of a loaded scene: visible or hidden, running or paused (frozen and kept in memory, resumed at once).

next_scene.description: 1.7: go to the scene that follows the current one (its next, else the next level); nothing at the end.

patch_data.description: 1.3 reaction: patch a document of a collection its kit declares moddable and live (the operations of a mod patch; values may be computed).

add_data.description: 1.3 reaction: add a document (its id must be free) to a moddable and live collection.

remove_data.description: 1.3 reaction: remove a document of a moddable and live collection.

set_config.description: 1.3 reaction: set a config path the kit declares moddable and live (validated against its configSchema).

set_setting.description: 1.3 reaction: change a live setting (<kit>.settings) the kit declares moddable.

set_component.description: 1.3 reaction: write a component a kit declares (engine.components), validated against its schema.

mod_enabled.description: A mod of this id is applied to the game.

weights.description: Shape name or index (as text) to a weight from 0 to 1; null removes a shape, {} removes them all.

set_morph.description: Sets the morph target weights of the model of an instance ({ "set_morph": { "smile": 0.6 }, "on": "curtain_1" }): kept with the instance, applied after the clips. An unknown instance or shape is a warning, once.

material.description: A name of the config's materials, a material, or null (back to the content's).

texture.description: Texture keys of the game (a path of its assets, or a slot it binds): color, normal, metallicRoughness (glTF: metal blue, roughness green).

set_material.description: 1.23: changes the material of an instance in place, over the one its content gives ({ "set_material": { "material": "gold" }, "on": "crate_1" }): kept with the instance and saved; the engine changes the drawn object's material, never makes it again.

game.end.description: The game is about to end with a result (won, lost or a custom one): a game or a mod changes the result or keeps the game running (a last chance, an epilogue first).

mission.complete.description: A mission is about to end (its last objective was just completed): a game or a mod changes the rewards, or refuses the end — the mission stays active, the objective that had just ended is armed again and mission.completion.refused says why.

reason.description: play, load_scene, next, enter, restart, push, pop.

loading.description: How the loading shows if the files are not ready: overlay, none, background or a scene id (mutable: another screen).

engine.scene.change.description: A scene change is about to happen (Play from the menu, load_scene, next_scene, push_scene, pop_scene, engine.scenes.enter): a game or a mod sends the player elsewhere (to, entry) or keeps them here (engine.scene.cancelled says by whom and why).

engine.scene.failed.description: Asked when files of the scene being loaded failed (each attempt): a game or a mod chooses what follows — retry them, enter without them, or wait (cancelled = wait) for engine.scenes.retry() or cancelLoading().

engine.scene.release.description: A scene was left and the memory of the files only it used is about to be freed (never the disk cache): a tap keeps some (assets: the ones still freed) or cancels (everything stays in memory, a scene the player comes back to at once).

engine.state.derive.description: A derived state of an instance is being computed (engine.content.states): value comes from its source (derived.var, derived.component, derived.expr; null for derived.hook); a game or a mod computes it instead. Never stored, saved, synced nor replayed.

archetype.description: Empty when the spec names none.

at.description: A point, { zone } or { entity, offset }.

engine.spawn.description: An entity is about to be created through spawn.try (a kit factory or the bare fallback): a game or a mod changes its archetype or its tags, or cancels the spawn — nothing is created and no entity id is consumed.

archetypes.description: Every kind of thing a scene places; { id, extends: "<archetype>" } inherits one and changes or adds what it writes (an interactable on a crate, another model).

game.engine.description: The engine contract kits require (game.engine@^1): version, active(), content, scenes, scripts, flow.

methods.name: active
methods.description: Returns whether game.engine is mounted and running for this game.

engine.sessions.description: Optional Rust KitHost service over gfsession. Not implemented by historical TS/Godot/Unity/Unreal game scripts. Read session-tools/README.md.

methods.name: create
methods.description: Create an explicitly owned decisions, timeline, replays, diagnostics or presentation instance.

methods.name: request
methods.description: Run a bounded Rust operation; failures are atomic. No automatic tick or gameplay save.

methods.name: remove
methods.description: Release the instance; the engine disposes its presentation resources.

methods.name: ids
methods.description: Deterministically list instances.

engine.flow.description: Game life cycle: phase(), start(scene?, entry?), end(result), restart(), result(). 1.1 (game.engine 1.9): with a title that shows the game (ui.menu titleMode scene), phase() is title until Play while the start scene is staged behind it, held.

methods.name: phase
methods.description: Returns the phase of the game: boot, title, playing or ended.

methods.name: start
methods.description: Starts the game in a scene (default the start scene).

methods.name: end
methods.description: Ends the game with a result, through the game.end hook.

methods.name: restart
methods.description: Resets the content state and enters the start scene again.

methods.name: result
methods.description: Returns the result the game ended with, or null.

engine.content.description: Content registry; placeGround(entity) queues a spawn query, with engine.placement.completed and engine.placement status/warnings. registerComponent(name, handler, kit), instances(scene?), instance(id) (with its talk topic), reflection(id), reflections(), entityOf(id), instanceOf(entity), archetype(id), state(id), setState(id, patch), report(), compiled(), active().

methods.name: placeGround
methods.description: Queue a downward physics query from the authored height after the collider is installed. Returns { pending: true }; engine.placement and engine.placement.completed report applied or skipped with warnings. No floor leaves the pose unchanged. Pending placement resumes after loading a save.

methods.name: registerComponent
methods.description: Registers the handler of a component a kit claims: called (entity, value, instance) for each instance that carries it.

methods.name: instances
methods.description: Returns the instances of a scene (default: the current scene).

methods.name: instance
methods.description: Returns one instance by id, with its talk topic, or null.

methods.name: reflection
methods.description: The look of an instance apart from its entity (docs/entites-et-rendu.md): { instance, entity, states (stored and derived), description (the content's model, the rules state → reflection, the bound values, what the display verbs set), resolved { model, components, visible, pose { rotation, scale, offset } }, bound [{ property, from, entity, render }] }; null without an entity. Never saved.

methods.name: reflections
methods.description: The description of the reflection of every instance that has an entity, by entity id: what a presentation module reads once when it starts after the scene.

methods.name: entityOf
methods.description: Returns the entity spawned for an instance id, or null.

methods.name: instanceOf
methods.description: Returns the instance id of an entity, or null.

methods.name: archetype
methods.description: Returns an archetype by id (inheritance already resolved), or null.

methods.name: state
methods.description: Returns the state of an instance (its state component and variables).

methods.name: states
methods.description: Returns the states of an instance: its stored states, then each derived state its archetype declares, computed now from its source and the engine.state.derive hook (never kept). Null for an unknown instance.

methods.name: setState
methods.description: Merges a patch into the state of an instance.

methods.name: setMaterial
methods.description: 1.23: the material of an instance (a name of the config's materials, a material, or null), changed in place (set_material).

methods.name: setFade
methods.description: The fade of an instance by its distance to the camera ({ start, end } in metres: whole beyond start, gone at end; start > end fades it as the camera comes near, start < end as it goes away; mode: alpha, a true opacity, the default, or dither, the engine's dither) or null (back to its content's fade). Written in model.fade, applied natively by every engine; nothing computed without it.

methods.name: report
methods.description: Returns the content report: errors and warnings of the compiled content.

methods.name: compiled
methods.description: Returns the compiled content (gripforge.engine/1): archetypes, instances, rules.

methods.name: active
methods.description: Returns whether a content (archetypes, scenes, scripts) is loaded.

engine.scenes.description: Scenes: current(), pending() (the scene the start will open, from setup), list(), enter(scene, entry?), visited(). sceneExit views carry next. 1.2 (game.engine 1.7): info(scene?) → { id, kind, role, next, title, loading, background, implicit, world, native, transition, below }, enter(scene, entry?, { unload, previous: { visible, paused } }) keeps the scene left loaded, push(scene, { entry, below, active }), pop(scene?), unload(scene), set(scene, { visible, paused }), stack(), active(), activate(scene), worldShown(), levels(), menu(), next(scene?), advance(entry?), loading() → { from, to, entry, ratio, since } | null, assets(scene?) (its scene_assets list, else computed). 1.3 (game.engine 1.11): native scenes, both ways — nativeEntered(path, { mode: replace | additive, kind, entry, assets }) → { scene, adopted, entered, known } (an engine adapter tells a native scene the game put in by itself; a path no document names is adopted as a scene of the game), nativeLeft(path), nativeAssets(scene, deps) (its files from the engine's dependency list), nativeScene(path) → scene id; info(scene).adopted. 1.4 (game.engine 1.19): the loading steps of the game — holdStep(id, { label?, scene?, timeout? }) (work of the game the kits cannot see, its terrain, its generation: without scene it holds the whole game, Play waits and a scene being entered waits behind its screen; with scene, or scene: "current", it holds that scene: its loading waits, and once entered its screen stays and entering() is true), stepProgress(id, ratio), releaseStep(id) → boolean, steps(scene?) → [{ id, label, scene, ratio }]; variable engine.steps { pending, game, ratio, label }; a step drops after its timeout (120 s by default).

methods.name: current
methods.description: Returns the current scene.

methods.name: pending
methods.description: Returns the scene the start will open (known from setup).

methods.name: list
methods.description: Returns every scene of the game.

methods.name: enter
methods.description: Leaves the current scene and enters another one at an entry.

methods.name: visited
methods.description: Returns the ids of the scenes already visited.

methods.name: info
methods.description: Returns the view of a scene (default: current): id, kind, role, next, title, loading, background, implicit, world, native, transition, below, adopted.

methods.name: push
methods.description: Adds a scene on top of the current one; below says what the scene under it does (run, pause, hide).

methods.name: pop
methods.description: Removes the top scene (or the one named) and gives the hand back to the scene below.

methods.name: unload
methods.description: Unloads a scene kept loaded and releases its assets.

methods.name: set
methods.description: Sets a loaded scene visible or hidden, running or paused.

methods.name: stack
methods.description: Returns the stack of the loaded scenes, bottom first.

methods.name: active
methods.description: Returns the id of the active scene (the one that receives the input).

methods.name: activate
methods.description: Makes a loaded scene the active one.

methods.name: worldShown
methods.description: Returns whether the world of a level is shown (false on an interface or loading scene).

methods.name: levels
methods.description: Returns the scenes of the level role, in order.

methods.name: menu
methods.description: Returns the menu scene of the scene flow, or null.

methods.name: next
methods.description: Returns the scene that follows a scene (default: current), from its next.

methods.name: advance
methods.description: Enters the scene that follows the current one, at an entry.

methods.name: loading
methods.description: Returns the loading in progress { from, to, entry, ratio, since }, or null.

methods.name: assets
methods.description: Returns the files of a scene: its scene_assets list, else computed from its content.

methods.name: nativeEntered
methods.description: Tells the engine a native scene the game put in by itself (replace or additive); a path no document names is adopted. Returns { scene, adopted, entered, known }.

methods.name: nativeLeft
methods.description: Tells the engine a native scene left.

methods.name: nativeAssets
methods.description: Gives the files of a scene from the dependency list of the engine.

methods.name: nativeScene
methods.description: Returns the scene id of a native scene path, or null.

methods.name: holdStep
methods.description: Holds the game (or a scene) behind its loading screen for work the kits cannot see, until releaseStep or its timeout (120 s).

methods.name: entering
methods.description: Returns whether a scene is being entered behind its loading screen.

methods.name: stepProgress
methods.description: Reports the progress of a held step, from 0 to 1.

methods.name: releaseStep
methods.description: Releases a held step; returns whether it was held.

methods.name: steps
methods.description: Returns the held steps [{ id, label, scene, ratio }], of a scene or all.

engine.scripts.description: Script verbs: registerAction(name, decl, fn, kit), registerCondition(…), verbs(), rules(), enable(script), disable(script), played().

methods.name: registerAction
methods.description: Registers an action verb of a kit: its declaration (schema) and its handler.

methods.name: registerCondition
methods.description: Registers a condition verb of a kit: its declaration (schema) and its handler.

methods.name: verbs
methods.description: Returns every verb known: engine verbs and the verbs of the kits.

methods.name: rules
methods.description: Returns the compiled rules of the scripts.

methods.name: enable
methods.description: Enables a script.

methods.name: disable
methods.description: Disables a script.

methods.name: played
methods.description: Returns the ids of the rules already played (the once rules).

engine.hooks.description: Interceptable decisions: decide(hook, payload) → { ok, payload, cancelled, reason, by, notes } (run is the same method), hold(hook, key, payload) / release(hook, key?) / held() for a continuous decision, tap(hook, fn, { priority, owner, id }) → id (an undeclared hook or a taken id is an error), untap(id) → bool, declare(hook, { mutable, cancellable, fields }, owner) (one owner per hook), declared(), taps(hook?), orphans(), problems(). Taps run by priority (higher first, 0 by default), then registration: the last has the final word, whoever registered it. Each tap sees the payload the previous ones left and the decision so far ({ cancelled, reason, by }, third argument); it answers { set, cancel: true|false, reason, stopImmediate }. Asked only when a tap listens.

methods.name: run
methods.description: The same method as decide (one answer, one short path when nobody listens).

methods.name: decide
methods.description: Asks every tap of a hook in order, on one payload; returns { ok, payload, cancelled, reason, by, notes }.

methods.name: hold
methods.description: Keeps the answer of a continuous decision until released (1.3).

methods.name: release
methods.description: Keeps the answer of a continuous decision until released (1.3).

methods.name: held
methods.description: Keeps the answer of a continuous decision until released (1.3).

methods.name: tap
methods.description: Adds a tap in code ({ priority, owner, id }); returns its id. Fails on a hook nobody declared and on a taken id (game code only, never a mod).

methods.name: untap
methods.description: Removes the tap in code of that id; returns whether it was there.

methods.name: declare
methods.description: Declares a hook ({ mutable, cancellable, fields }) owned by one kit or the game; fails when another owner has it.

methods.name: declared
methods.description: Lists the declared hooks with their owner.

methods.name: taps
methods.description: Lists the taps, of one hook or all.

methods.name: orphans
methods.description: Lists the taps on a hook nobody declares (never asked).

methods.name: problems
methods.description: Lists what is wrong with the hooks: declared by two kits, data taps on undeclared hooks or on hooks denied to mods.

engine.mods.description: The mods the game was mounted with: list(), applied(), has(id), originOf(collection, id), fingerprint() (1.3: a stable string for the mods applied and their content, '' without a mod; network kits compare it in their handshake).

methods.name: list
methods.description: Returns every mod with its status (applied, disabled, refused) and issues / only the mods applied, in order.

methods.name: applied
methods.description: Returns every mod with its status (applied, disabled, refused) and issues / only the mods applied, in order.

methods.name: has
methods.description: Returns whether a mod of this id is applied.

methods.name: originOf
methods.description: Returns the mod that added a document of a collection, or null for the project own documents.

methods.name: fingerprint
methods.description: Returns a stable string of the mods applied (empty without a mod), compared by network kits.

engine.points.description: 1.3: what can be plugged into a kit, names only (hooks, events emitted and listened, registries, collections, config, moddable and live, settings, verbs, components, services, completeness counts): list() for the installed kits, of(kit) for any kit of the catalogue. The full view with schemas is extensionPointsOf(manifest).

methods.name: list
methods.description: Returns the extension points of the installed kits, names only.

methods.name: of
methods.description: Returns the extension points of one kit of the catalogue, names only.

methods.name: extensionPointsOf
methods.description: Returns the full extension points of a manifest, with their schemas.

world.zones.description: Named zones exist without a world kit: the scene zones and the project zones collection, in the host zones (ctx.zones). No service of its own: a world kit that also provides world.zones (city block, district, rooms) serves its view.

engine.debug.description: The reads of game.engine's debugger entries (expose, for debug). JSON, rare: only an open panel or an agent's snapshot reads them, and again only when epoch() moves. Each method can be served by the game in its language (provide_<method>).

methods.name: epoch
methods.description: A number that moves when the scenes, instances, journal or loading change: the debugger reads the other methods again only then.

methods.name: scenes
methods.description: The scenes: current, the stack (each layer with its state visible/paused, its info and its number of files), every scene of the game (all) and the phase of the flow.

methods.name: instances
methods.description: The instances spawned by game.engine: count and up to 512 rows { instance, entity, borrowed, archetype, kind, scene } (the object card of the panel: what it is, where it comes from).

methods.name: vars
methods.description: The variables game.engine defines: engine.scene, engine.scene.kind, engine.scene.loading, engine.scene.world and the story flags.

methods.name: hooks
methods.description: The hooks of the game: declared, the taps on them and the answers held (engine.hooks).

methods.name: mods
methods.description: The mods of the game: the list and those applied (engine.mods).

methods.name: archetypes
methods.description: The archetypes of the game: up to 512 rows { id, kind, asset, components (their names), instances (how many spawned) }: the groups of objects the panel hides or shows together, and the archetype part of an object's card.

methods.name: reflections
methods.description: Each value of an instance on both sides (docs/entites-et-rendu.md, rule 5): for the instance asked, else for those whose look follows a table (reflect rules, bound values) or was set at run time, at most 32. { count, rows: [{ instance, entity, visible, values: [{ property, entity, render, link }] }] }, link: bound (root) for the position and yaw, bound, free (drawn only: scale, material), stored state, derived state (read only). Read by an open panel only, at each of its periods (no epoch).
